look_here_first: Start with the glossy leaves and the narrower pink-to-red corolla. Hill Country penstemon is an erect perennial with opposite dark-green leaves; lower leaves are often toothed while upper leaves become smaller and more entire/connate. Flowers are usually about 25–35 mm, distinctly smaller than P. cobaea.

lookalikes.differences: Penstemon cobaea: P. cobaea has much larger 35–55 mm pale flowers with a strongly inflated throat and broader serrate leaves. Penstemon baccharifolius: P. baccharifolius is a woody-based low subshrub with thick leathery serrate leaves and red flowers from cliff/rock crevices. Penstemon tenuis: P. tenuis has tiny 10–14 mm lavender flowers, sharp small calyx lobes and a wetter coastal/alluvial ecology.
